[Chapter 2](02_simulation_runs_and_replications.qmd) ended with each replication getting its own seed from the master seed. This chapter picks that seed up inside the model and follows it into `Utils`.

## What it is {#sec-sampling-distributions-and-random-streams-what-it-is}

`Utils` (in `air_ambulance_des/utils.py`) is the model's sampling layer. Its constructor reads every fitted input the model needs from `distribution_data/` (plus `upper_allowable_time_bounds.csv` from `actual_data/`) into pandas frames and dictionaries. After `setup_seeds()` it exposes selection methods (`ampds_code_selection`, `care_category_selection`, `activity_time`, `inc_per_day_samples`, `sample_ad_hoc_reason` and friends) that each return one sampled value.

The contract callers rely on:

- **Input:** a `SeedSequence` (the `master_seed` argument) and the files in `distribution_data/`, which [Distribution Fitting](08_distribution_fitting.qmd) produces.
- **Output:** one value per call, drawn from a stream named for the purpose, so the same seed always gives the same sequence for that purpose.
- **Invariant:** each sampling purpose has its own `numpy` `Generator`. Drawing more or fewer values for one purpose must not move the numbers any other purpose sees.
- **Callers:** `DES_HEMS` builds one `Utils` per run ([Calls and Patient Journeys](04_calls_and_patient_journeys.qmd)). `HEMSAvailability` receives that same object and calls `sample_ad_hoc_reason` during allocation ([Resource Allocation](06_resource_allocation.qmd)).

The use case this chapter keeps returning to: a patient's mobile time is sampled with `activity_time("helicopter", "time_mobile")`, and you want it to be reproducible and unaffected by someone adding a new sampled attribute elsewhere.

`Utils` also carries unrelated odds and ends: folder constants, school-holiday date calculators, and module-level helpers such as `format_diff` and `get_rota_month_strings`. They are out of scope here except where they bite (see @sec-sampling-distributions-and-random-streams-sharp-edges).

## How it works {#sec-sampling-distributions-and-random-streams-how-it-works}

### Construction and seeding

`DES_HEMS.__init__` turns the run's integer seed into a `SeedSequence`, spawns one child for `Utils`, and calls `setup_seeds()` straight away.

```{.python include="../../../air_ambulance_des/des_hems.py" start-line=61 end-line=71 filename="air_ambulance_des/des_hems.py:61-71" code-line-style="focus:2,6-9" include-hash="378204b19b49"}
```

So the seed chain from [Chapter 2](02_simulation_runs_and_replications.qmd) is: master seed, then per-run seed (integer), then a `SeedSequence` per model, then one child per `Utils`, then one stream per purpose (@fig-sampling-utils-seed-tree).

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-sampling-utils-seed-tree
%%| fig-cap: "Seed hierarchy inside one run"
flowchart TD
    A["random_seed (int, per run)"] --> B["SeedSequence(random_seed)"]
    B -->|"spawn(1)[0]"| C["Utils.master_seed_sequence"]
    C -->|"spawn(22) in setup_seeds"| D["22 named Generators in Utils.rngs"]
    C -->|"spawn(n) in build_seeded_distributions"| E["one Generator per activity-time fit"]
    E --> F["SeededDistribution"]
```

`setup_seeds()` does the spawning:

```{.python include="../../../air_ambulance_des/utils.py" start-line=184 end-line=221 filename="air_ambulance_des/utils.py:184-221" code-line-style="focus:32-38" include-hash="4d49571d280b"}
```

`SeedSequence.spawn` is stateful: it hands out children numbered from an internal counter. That is why the second `spawn` inside `build_seeded_distributions` (called on the last line above) gives the activity-time generators streams that differ from the 22 named ones, without any extra bookkeeping.

### Weighted table lookups

Most selection methods follow one pattern: filter a probability table by the conditioning variables, then draw one row with `proportion` as weights, passing the named generator as `random_state`.

```{.python include="../../../air_ambulance_des/utils.py" start-line=289 end-line=301 filename="air_ambulance_des/utils.py:289-301" code-line-style="focus:8-12" include-hash="f1231ffc31e9"}
```

`care_category_selection`, `pt_outcome_selection`, `callsign_group_selection`, `vehicle_type_selection_qtr` and the HEMS result sampler `Utils.hems_results_by_patient_outcome_and_time_of_day_and_quarter_and_vehicle_type_and_callsign_group_probs` are the same shape with different filters and different stream keys. Two methods deviate: `sex_selection` compares `rngs["sex_selection"].uniform(0, 1)` with a single probability, and `sample_ad_hoc_reason` uses `Generator.choice` with normalised probabilities.

### Continuous distributions and activity times

The files `activity_time_distributions.txt`, `age_distributions.txt` and the two `inc_per_day_*` files hold Python literals, read with `ast.literal_eval` in the constructor. Activity times are special: `build_seeded_distributions` replaces `self.activity_time_distr` with a dictionary of `SeededDistribution` objects, keyed by `(vehicle_type, time_type)`.

```{.python include="../../../air_ambulance_des/utils.py" start-line=890 end-line=955 filename="air_ambulance_des/utils.py:890-955" code-line-style="focus:13-14,62,64" code-window-collapse="closed" include-hash="464164a16540"}
```

Each fitted entry is looked up in a name-to-scipy-class map (`dist_map`). Unknown names raise `ValueError`; `exponential` and `normal` are aliases. The generator for entry *i* is the *i*-th spawned child, so the order of entries in `activity_time_distributions.txt` decides which entry gets which stream.

`SeededDistribution` is a thin pair of a frozen scipy distribution and its generator:

```{.python include="../../../air_ambulance_des/utils.py" start-line=1053 end-line=1059 filename="air_ambulance_des/utils.py:1053-1059" include-hash="8851c40572cc"}
```

`activity_time` then draws from it, rejecting values outside the bounds for that `time_type`:

```{.python include="../../../air_ambulance_des/utils.py" start-line=580 end-line=607 filename="air_ambulance_des/utils.py:580-607" code-line-style="focus:22-24" include-hash="2dd439897db1"}
```

The bounds come from `min_max_cache`, built in the constructor from `upper_allowable_time_bounds.csv`:

```{.python include="../../../air_ambulance_des/utils.py" start-line=177 end-line=182 filename="air_ambulance_des/utils.py:177-182" include-hash="c3d850dc576e"}
```

Note the lookup is by `time_type` only. The bounds are shared across vehicle types.

Ages and daily call counts use the other path, `sample_from_distribution`, which takes a one-entry dict such as `{"gamma": {...}}` and the stream to use:

```{.python include="../../../air_ambulance_des/utils.py" start-line=673 end-line=698 filename="air_ambulance_des/utils.py:673-698" code-line-style="focus:23-26" include-hash="3c9b73dd308f"}
```

It floors the draw and loops until the result is positive. `age_sampling` and `inc_per_day` wrap it in further loops (a maximum age; per-season or per-quarter min and max counts).

The model itself calls `inc_per_day_samples`, not `inc_per_day`. It resamples from empirical daily counts stored in `inc_per_day_samples.json`:

```{.python include="../../../air_ambulance_des/utils.py" start-line=652 end-line=671 filename="air_ambulance_des/utils.py:652-671" code-line-style="focus:14-16,18-20" include-hash="09d9a441494d"}
```

`quarter_or_season` picks the JSON key (`"summer"`/`"winter"` or `"Q1"` to `"Q4"`). `DES_HEMS` sets `daily_calls_by_quarter_or_season = "quarter"` (`des_hems.py:76`), so the quarter keys are the live path; the season default here is not what the model uses.

### Ad hoc unavailability

`sample_ad_hoc_reason(hour, quarter, registration)` maps the hour to a six-hour bin, filters `ad_hoc_unavailability.csv` by registration, bin and quarter, and falls back in stages:

1. no rows for that registration: use all registrations for that bin and quarter;
2. still none: return `"available"`;
3. any NaN probability: impute the registration's mean across bins for that reason, else the bin's mean across registrations, else return `"available"`;
4. probabilities still missing or summing to zero: return `"available"`.

Only then does it normalise and draw:

```{.python include="../../../air_ambulance_des/utils.py" start-line=1044 end-line=1050 filename="air_ambulance_des/utils.py:1044-1050" include-hash="09f78e630475"}
```

Every degraded path returns `"available"`, so missing data silently makes aircraft more available. The constructor is consistent with this: if `ad_hoc_unavailability.csv` is absent, the `FileNotFoundError` is caught (`utils.py:131-138`) and `self.ad_hoc_probs` is simply never set. The failure then surfaces as an `AttributeError` at the first call, not at construction.

## Extending this {#sec-sampling-distributions-and-random-streams-extending-this}

**Add a new sampled quantity (a new probability table).**

1. Produce the CSV in `DistributionFitUtils` ([Distribution Fitting](08_distribution_fitting.qmd)), writing to `distribution_data/`.
2. Load it in `Utils.__init__` next to the others.
3. Add a key to `module_keys` in `setup_seeds` **at the end of the list**. See the first sharp edge below for why.
4. Write the selection method following `ampds_code_selection`: filter, then `pd.Series.sample(..., random_state=self.rngs["<key>"])`.
5. Call it from `DES_HEMS` ([Calls and Patient Journeys](04_calls_and_patient_journeys.qmd)).

**Add a new activity time or vehicle type.** Add the fit in the activity-time distributions file via the fitting pipeline, and add a row for the `time_type` in `upper_allowable_time_bounds.csv`. `activity_time` raises `ValueError` for a missing distribution or missing bounds. A new scipy family must be added to `dist_map` in `build_seeded_distributions`.

**Change which file backs a sampler** (for example per-season versus per-quarter call counts): the switch is `daily_calls_by_quarter_or_season` on `DES_HEMS`. The JSON must have the matching keys.

**Conventions the code expects**

- One stream key per sampling purpose, and the method reads `self.rngs[<key>]`. Keys are strings, so a typo is a `KeyError` at the first sample.
- Probability tables have a `proportion` column. Method-specific filter columns are named in the existing methods.
- Tests that exercise sampling construct `Utils(master_seed=SeedSequence(42))` and call `setup_seeds()` explicitly (`tests/test_resource_allocation.py:34-35`).

**Tests that cover this area:** `tests/test_reproducibility.py`, `tests/test_against_reality.py`, `tests/test_backtest.py` and `tests/test_resource_allocation.py`. The repo's `tests/README.md` documents running them from the repo root:

```{.bash .illustrative filename="Example usage (see tests/README.md)"}
pytest tests/test_reproducibility.py
pytest tests/test_resource_allocation.py
pytest -m backtest
```

If a change to sampling is meant to alter results, `tests/README.md` describes `pytest -m backtest --update-backtest-baseline` for refreshing the stored baseline after you have checked the differences.

## Sharp edges {#sec-sampling-distributions-and-random-streams-sharp-edges}

- **Inserting a stream key shifts everyone after it.** Children are numbered by position in `spawn(len(module_keys))`, and the activity-time generators are spawned afterwards from the same sequence. Adding a key anywhere moves the activity-time streams, and adding one mid-list also moves the later named streams. Results change even for a fixed seed. This follows from how `SeedSequence.spawn` works; the repo does not say it in a comment (inferred).
- **`setup_seeds()` is not idempotent.** `build_seeded_distributions` overwrites `self.activity_time_distr` (a list of dicts) with a dict. A second call would iterate the dict's tuple keys and fail on `entry["vehicle_type"]`.
- **The default `master_seed=SeedSequence(42)` is evaluated once, at function definition.** Every `Utils()` that uses the default shares one `SeedSequence` object and its spawn counter. Two such objects do not get identical streams.
- **Bare `Utils()` objects have no streams.** `HEMS` objects ([Chapter 5](05_hems_resources_and_servicing.qmd)) each build a bare `Utils()` for their time-range helper (`class_hems.py:33`). It has no `rngs` because `setup_seeds()` is never called, so never sample from it.
- **Import-time file reads.** `HEMS_ROTA`, `HEMS_ROTA_DEFAULT` and `SERVICING_SCHEDULES_BY_MODEL` are read when the module is imported (`utils.py:49-56`), not when `Utils` is constructed. The app overwrites those CSVs ([Streamlit App and Scenario Parameters](01_streamlit_app_and_scenario_parameters.qmd)), so a process that imported `utils` earlier holds the old class-level frames. `Utils.__init__` itself reads `distribution_data/` fresh each time.
- **Rejection loops have no cap.** `activity_time`, `sample_from_distribution`, `age_sampling` and `inc_per_day` loop until a draw lands in range. Bounds that the fitted distribution almost never reaches will hang a run rather than raise.
- **Stale-looking `TODO: RANDOM SEED SETTING`** comments sit above `sex_selection` and `age_sampling` (`utils.py:535`, `:552`), yet both already use named streams. Whatever they originally flagged, the current code is seeded.
- **Ad hoc fallbacks are silent.** See above: every degraded path returns `"available"`, and `sample_ad_hoc_reason` is annotated `-> bool` while returning a string.
- **Hour ranges are inclusive in one place.** `hems_results_by_patient_outcome_and_time_of_day_and_quarter_and_vehicle_type_and_callsign_group_probs` treats hours 7 to 18 inclusive as `"day"`, so a call at 18:xx is day; `sample_ad_hoc_reason` uses different, six-hour bins.
- **Two methods lack `self`.** `Utils.current_time()` and `Utils.biased_mean(series, bias)` are defined without `self`, so they only work when called on the class, not an instance. Commit `7f5798f` notes `biased_mean` "may need watching".

## Design notes {#sec-sampling-distributions-and-random-streams-design-notes}

**Documented.**

- Random number streams for activity times were introduced in commit `2af661f`, and commit `9a05b28` moved seed handling to numpy seed sequences "more robustly". Together these are the origin of the `SeedSequence` plus named-generator design.
- Commit `2eb0ffd` fixed different results in tests where a seed was set, which is the behaviour `tests/test_reproducibility.py` now guards.
- Commit `7f5798f` added the option to stratify calls per day by season or quarter, which is the `quarter_or_season` argument.
- Commit `ceb157e` switched vehicle type sampling to per quarter, which is why `vehicle_type_selection_qtr` is live and the non-quarter version is commented out.
- Commit `5ad2dec` moved `utils.py` into the `air_ambulance_des` package; file history before that move was not followed.

**Inferred.**

- The named-stream split presumably exists so that changing one part of the model (say, adding a sampled field) does not reshuffle unrelated draws, which makes scenario comparisons less noisy. The code is consistent with that but no commit message says so.
- Pairing each scipy distribution with its own generator in `SeededDistribution` suggests the aim of keeping every `(vehicle_type, time_type)` fit independent of how many times the others are drawn.
- The large block of commented-out methods and `# ARCHIVED CODE` suggests the sampling tables were reworked more than once; the live versions are the quarter-stratified ones. This is a reading of the code only.

## Limitations and open questions {#sec-sampling-distributions-and-random-streams-limitations}

- Issue [#183](https://github.com/RichardPilbery/DAA_DES/issues/183) (open as of 2026-10-19): add tests to quantify how much the random seed matters.
- Issue [#241](https://github.com/RichardPilbery/DAA_DES/issues/241) (open as of 2026-10-19): a car is sometimes sent when the ad hoc unavailability spreadsheet gives no obvious reason, which touches the sampling fallbacks above.
- The two `TODO: RANDOM SEED SETTING` markers at `air_ambulance_des/utils.py:535` and `:552`.

Check the [issue tracker](https://github.com/RichardPilbery/DAA_DES/issues) for the current state.

## Conclusion

With sampling and seeding in hand, [Calls and Patient Journeys](04_calls_and_patient_journeys.qmd) shows where `DES_HEMS` calls these methods as each call becomes a patient.
